narrativeReportMd:
# Element R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard instance-breaking change was found for local `Element` content: `Element`, `Element.id`, and `Element.extension` are still present with the same paths, cardinalities, primary types, modifier flags, summary flags, and extension slicing. The main migration concerns are runtime/codegen concerns in infrastructure tooling rather than ordinary instance shape changes.

## Scope
This analysis covers the core `Element` StructureDefinition in R4 4.0.1 and R6 6.0.0-ballot4. Because `Element` itself is the assigned base/infrastructure artifact, the new explicit relationship to `Base` is in scope. Changes inherited by derived resources/datatypes, changes inside `Extension`, and downstream class hierarchy impacts are delegated to the relevant artifact reports.

## Main migration themes
R6 makes the FHIR type system hierarchy more explicit by declaring `Element` as a specialization of `Base`. R6 also keeps the universal `ele-1` FHIRPath expression but no longer supplies XPath constraint metadata and changes condition metadata placement. Finally, `Element.extension` no longer carries the `Extension`-owned `ext-1` invariant inline in the Element snapshot, so validators need to validate through the referenced `Extension` type instead of relying only on copied usage-site constraints.

## Highest-impact findings
All findings are Medium or lower. The most important operational issue is for generated models, validators, schema emitters, and cross-version conversion code that assumed R4's root `Element` hierarchy or that depended on XPath/inlined constraints in the Element snapshot.

## Findings requiring human review
The `Element.extension` usage-site constraint change deserves review because the computable R6 `Extension` definition still has `ext-1`; the risk is likely packaging/tooling behavior rather than a normative permission to create invalid extensions.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most changes look like infrastructure cleanup or clarification. Backward compatibility could have been improved by retaining transitional metadata such as `xpath` and usage-site `ext-1` copies, but those alternatives would preserve old tooling habits rather than changing the instance model.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the `Base` and `Extension` reports together with this one. Derived datatype/resource reports should not duplicate the Element-level class hierarchy and universal invariant findings.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No local hard instance-breaking Element shape change was found. The top migration concerns are the new explicit `Base` superclass, the loss of XPath constraint metadata for `ele-1`, and the need to follow the `Extension` type to enforce `ext-1` rather than relying on Element's usage-site snapshot. The main uncertainty is whether the `Element.extension` constraint-packaging difference is documented as intentional in narrative or migration notes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is primarily about infrastructure tooling. Generated class hierarchies should account for `Base -> Element`; validators and schema generators should use FHIRPath constraints rather than XPath; and validation of `Element.extension` should dereference and apply the `Extension` StructureDefinition rather than assuming every relevant constraint is copied into the Element snapshot element.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the direct computable deltas because both StructureDefinitions and package indexes were inspected. Confidence is medium for the rationale and expected implementation impact because no official diff, full narrative migration guidance, or ballot/Jira rationale was reviewed. No terminology uncertainty affects this artifact because Element has no bindings.

findings.title: Element now explicitly specializes the new Base type

oldState.summary: R4 Element is the root Element infrastructure type and does not declare baseDefinition or derivation.

semanticText.definition: Base definition for all elements in a resource.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 `Element` StructureDefinition has the same canonical URL and abstract complex-type identity, but no `baseDefinition` or `derivation` field. R4 package indexing also has no `StructureDefinition-Base.json` counterpart.

newState.summary: R6 Element keeps the same canonical identity but declares baseDefinition Base and derivation specialization.

semanticText.definition: Base definition for all elements in a resource.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 `Element` StructureDefinition declares `baseDefinition: http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Base` and `derivation: specialization`. The R6 package includes `StructureDefinition-Base.json`, whose root is an abstract `Base` type for all FHIR types and resources.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The artifact itself was matched by exact canonical URL, id, name, type, kind, and abstract flag. The difference is not a rename or split; it is an explicit superclass relationship added around the same Element identity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This does not add or remove serialized instance elements, so ordinary R4 Element content does not become invalid merely because of the new superclass. The risk is in generated code, reflection models, visitor hierarchies, validators, and converters that assumed `Element` was the top of the FHIR object hierarchy or that keyed behavior on a missing `baseDefinition`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is primarily implementation breakage or incomplete validation/conversion behavior, not a direct clinical semantic change in Element instances.

justification.inferredGoal: Make the FHIR type system root explicit and align Element with the R6 Base infrastructure type.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep Element as the formal root and describe Base as narrative or auxiliary tooling metadata instead of a computable superclass.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R6 makes the common FHIR type-system root explicit by adding `Base` and declaring `Element` as its specialization. That is a real computable-model change rather than an instance-shape change, and it can break generators or reflection code that assumed `Element` was root. A less-breaking design exists only in a partial sense because leaving `Element` root would avoid old tooling churn but would leave the R6 hierarchy less explicit and less uniform.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking alternative would have been to retain the R4 formal shape, with `Element` having no `baseDefinition`, and document `Base` as a conceptual or auxiliary implementation root. That preserves most existing code-generation assumptions, but it fails the strongest version of the R6 goal: a computable `Base -> Element` hierarchy in the core StructureDefinitions. Because the alternative is incomplete rather than an equivalent low-cost design, the break is probably justified.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves the R4 hierarchy for older generators but does not fully meet the R6 goal of a formal, uniform Base type.

evidence.detail: R4 Element has no baseDefinition field.
R6 Base is present as an abstract complex-type with description 'Base definition for all types defined in FHIR type system.'.

examples.examplesMd: No old-valid/new-invalid JSON instance fragment is expected from this hierarchy change alone; the affected artifacts are generated classes, validators, converters, and reflection metadata.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 preserves the `Element` artifact identity but inserts an explicit `Base` superclass above it. This can surprise infrastructure implementations because R4 code often treats Element as the root for all element-like model objects. The serialized shape of `Element.id` and `Element.extension` is unchanged, but generated inheritance, type switches, and cross-version mappers may need to be regenerated or adjusted.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance does not become R6-invalid simply because `Element` now specializes `Base`; `Base` has no additional serialized children in the inspected R6 StructureDefinition. R6 content also does not become unrepresentable in R4 at the JSON/XML instance level for this reason alone. The compatibility issue is runtime metadata: code that expects `Element.baseDefinition` to be absent or that assumes no superclass above Element can fail or skip Base-level processing.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate model classes and validators from the R6 StructureDefinitions, and explicitly test type traversal from `Base` to `Element` to concrete datatypes/resources. Cross-version converters should not serialize `Base` as an extra instance element; it is a model hierarchy concept. Reflection code should handle both the R4 no-base case and the R6 `Base` superclass case.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The less disruptive option would have been to keep Element as the formal root and document Base separately, but that would preserve an implicit hierarchy. Adding `Base` is probably justified for uniform R6 infrastructure, provided generators and migration guidance make the non-serialized nature of the change clear.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the Element canonical and serialized local shape, but inserts a computable Base superclass above Element. A model generator, validator, or reflection API that assumed Element had no parent can need code changes, so this is a real infrastructure compatibility issue. It does not make existing Element instance content invalid, and the R6 goal of an explicit common root for FHIR types and resources is coherent enough that the hierarchy change looks proportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-Element.json has no baseDefinition or derivation.
R6 StructureDefinition-Element.json declares baseDefinition http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Base and derivation specialization.
R6 StructureDefinition-Base.json is an abstract complex-type with no serialized child elements in the inspected root.
Package indexes show Base absent in R4 and present in R6.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Element is normative in R4, so a superclass/API change deserves stronger justification. That raised scrutiny, but the absence of an instance-shape change and the plausible type-system rationale kept the judgment below Revisit.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: generated inheritance, type traversal, reflection metadata, or validators keyed to Element as the root can break; no old-valid/new-invalid instance mechanism was found.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have left Element as the formal root and documented Base conceptually, but that would not provide the same computable Base-to-Element hierarchy. A deprecated alias concept is not very applicable to a superclass edge, so there is no clean low-cost base design that both preserves R4 tooling assumptions and meets the R6 goal.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing no-hard-break and medium runtime-impact assessment, and broadly agree that the alternative is only partial rather than a clearly less-breaking equivalent.

findings.title: The universal ele-1 invariant is FHIRPath-only in the R6 Element definition

oldState.summary: R4 Element carries ele-1 with a FHIRPath expression and XPath metadata; root condition lists ele-1.

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `Element` includes `ele-1` as an error invariant with FHIRPath expression `hasValue() or (children().count() > id.count())` and XPath `@value|f:*|h:div`. The root ElementDefinition also lists condition `ele-1`.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the ele-1 FHIRPath expression but removes XPath metadata, clarifies the human text, and places condition ele-1 on Element.id rather than the root.

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children or both

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `ele-1` remains an error invariant with the same FHIRPath expression. The XPath form is absent, the human description explicitly says 'or both', the constraint has an explicit Element source, and `Element.id` carries condition `ele-1` while the root no longer lists the condition.

facts.note: R6 no longer provides XPath metadata for the invariant.

facts.oldValue: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children
facts.newValue: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children or both

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The invariant is matched by stable key `ele-1` and identical FHIRPath expression. The material difference is metadata representation, not the logical validation test.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The same FHIRPath expression means properly implemented R4 and R6 validators should accept and reject the same Element content for `ele-1`. However, validators, schema generators, documentation tooling, or code generators that consumed `constraint.xpath` or inferred affected elements from `condition` metadata must change behavior for R6.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The invariant itself is unchanged, so no direct clinical or business semantic change was identified.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify ele-1 wording and rely on the normative FHIRPath expression rather than carrying XPath metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated or informational XPath constraint metadata during a transition while keeping FHIRPath as the normative expression.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The validation rule itself is unchanged because R6 keeps the same `ele-1` FHIRPath expression, so this is not an R4-valid to R6-invalid instance break. The break is for tooling that depended on `constraint.xpath` or old condition placement. Retaining XPath would have been less disruptive, but R6 also removes `ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath` from the metamodel, so preserving compatibility would require carrying deprecated duplicate constraint representations beyond this one Element definition. That material tradeoff makes the FHIRPath-only design probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept `constraint.xpath` as deprecated or informational metadata while declaring FHIRPath to be the source of truth and clarifying the human text. This would preserve older XPath-based validators for common cases. It is only a partial alternative because maintaining two expression forms globally risks stale or inconsistent invariants and undercuts the apparent R6 goal of removing XPath from core computable definitions.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Eases XPath-only tooling migration but preserves a duplicate expression language that R6 removed from the ElementDefinition constraint model.

evidence.detail: R4 ele-1 has the same FHIRPath expression plus XPath metadata.
R6 ele-1 keeps the FHIRPath expression and has no xpath property.
R4 root ElementDefinition lists condition ele-1.
R6 Element.id lists condition ele-1 while the root ElementDefinition condition list is absent.

examples.examplesMd: No old-valid/new-invalid instance example is expected because the FHIRPath expression is unchanged. A tooling example would be an XPath-only validator that can enforce R4 `ele-1` from `constraint.xpath` but cannot load the R6 invariant unless it supports FHIRPath.

findings.narrativeMd: The universal `ele-1` invariant did not become stricter, but its computable packaging changed. R6 removes the XPath representation and clarifies the human wording to include 'or both'. This matters for validators and schema emitters that treated XPath as the executable rule or used `condition` metadata for dependency analysis. Such tools may appear to lose the universal Element invariant unless they execute FHIRPath and read constraints directly.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: For validators that execute FHIRPath, an R4-valid Element does not become invalid in R6 and an R6-valid Element does not become unrepresentable in R4 because the expression is identical. For XPath-only or condition-driven tooling, the R6 definition can be a runtime break: the invariant is still present, but not in the old metadata location/form.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Migrate validation engines to use `constraint.expression` FHIRPath as the source of truth. Do not treat the missing `xpath` property as removal of `ele-1`. Test empty elements, primitive values with extensions, and elements with only `id` to confirm the R6 validator still enforces `hasValue() or (children().count() > id.count())`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The semantic goal was achievable without breaking XPath-based tooling by retaining `constraint.xpath` as deprecated or informational metadata. The tradeoff is that retaining XPath would increase maintenance burden and risk inconsistency between XPath and FHIRPath. Because the validation expression is unchanged, the compatibility issue is avoidable but limited to tooling, not data instances.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The executable ele-1 FHIRPath test is unchanged, so a conformant FHIRPath-based validator should accept and reject the same Element content. The compatibility issue is for older tooling that used the R4 XPath copy or the old condition placement as the computable hook for the invariant. That is migration work for validators and schema emitters, but relying on one canonical FHIRPath expression in R6 is a reasonable cleanup and avoids maintaining duplicate constraint languages.
keyEvidence: R4 Element.constraint[ele-1] expression is hasValue() or (children().count() > id.count()) and includes xpath @value|f:*|h:div.
R6 Element.constraint[ele-1] keeps the same FHIRPath expression, changes the human text to include 'or both', and has no xpath property.
R4 root Element lists condition ele-1; R6 places condition ele-1 on Element.id.
R4 ElementDefinition includes ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath; R6 ElementDefinition.constraint children no longer include xpath.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Element is normative, which makes removal of computable metadata worth checking carefully. The stability concern is softened by the identical validation expression and by the broader R6 metamodel change away from XPath.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: XPath-only or condition-driven validation/code generation can fail to carry forward ele-1, but base instance validity is unchanged when constraint.expression is used.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained xpath as deprecated informational metadata, or kept the old condition placement for a transition. That would help legacy tools but would preserve duplicate expression forms after R6 removed xpath from ElementDefinition.constraint, increasing divergence and source-of-truth risk.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing medium tooling-impact assessment; the fresh review gives more weight to the unchanged FHIRPath expression and treats the less-breaking option as costly transitional metadata rather than a strong alternative.

findings.title: Element.extension no longer carries the Extension-owned ext-1 invariant inline in the Element snapshot

oldState.summary: R4 Element.extension snapshot includes both ele-1 and ext-1 constraints; ext-1 comes from Extension.

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children
Must have either extensions or value[x], not both

slicing.description: Extensions are always sliced by (at least) url

oldState.narrativeMd: In the R4 Element snapshot, the `Element.extension` element is typed as `Extension` and the snapshot includes the Extension-owned `ext-1` invariant, prohibiting a single extension from having both nested `extension` children and a `value[x]`.

newState.summary: R6 Element.extension snapshot includes ele-1 but not an inline ext-1 constraint; the R6 Extension root still defines ext-1.

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

slicing.description: Extensions are always sliced by (at least) url

newState.narrativeMd: In the R6 Element snapshot, `Element.extension` still has type `Extension` and unchanged slicing/cardinality, but the inline `ext-1` constraint is no longer copied onto this usage site. The R6 `Extension` StructureDefinition itself still carries `ext-1` at its root.

facts.note: R6 Extension root still defines ext-1; the change is in Element's usage-site snapshot.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element is matched by the same id/path `Element.extension`, same type `Extension`, and same cardinality/slicing. The difference is the set of constraints included in the Element snapshot for that usage site.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A conformant R6 validator that validates the child against the `Extension` StructureDefinition should still enforce `ext-1`, so this is not evidence that R6 permits extensions with both nested extensions and a value. The risk is for snapshot-only validators, code generators, or schema emitters that relied on R4's copied usage-site constraint and do not dereference the `Extension` type.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If a validator misses `ext-1`, malformed extensions could be accepted, which can affect extension interpretation. The risk is mitigated because the R6 Extension definition still carries the invariant.

justification.inferredGoal: Avoid duplicating type-owned constraints at every usage site in snapshots, or reflect changed snapshot-generation rules.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Continue inlining the Extension-owned `ext-1` constraint on `Element.extension` as transitional snapshot metadata while keeping `Extension` as the source definition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The likely R6 goal is to compose validation through the declared `Extension` type instead of copying every type-owned invariant onto each usage site. That goal is reasonable, and valid instance semantics are not intended to weaken because the R6 `Extension` StructureDefinition still defines `ext-1`. The break is limited to snapshot-only validators and schema emitters that relied on the R4 copied constraint. A less-breaking inlining strategy exists, but its duplication and authority tradeoffs are material enough that the cleanup is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking design would keep the R4-style inline `ext-1` copy on `Element.extension`, perhaps marked as inherited or informational, so older snapshot-only tooling continues to reject extensions with both nested `extension` and `value[x]`. This would preserve old behavior for common tooling patterns, but it is not a clean equivalent design: duplicated constraints can diverge from the source `Extension` rule, make it unclear whether usage-site snapshots or type definitions are authoritative, and encourage validators not to dereference the declared type.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Helps snapshot-only validators but duplicates type-owned rules and creates stale-copy and source-of-truth ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 Element.extension includes ext-1 with source Extension.
R6 Element.extension includes ele-1 but no ext-1 inline constraint.
R6 Extension root still defines ext-1 as an error invariant.
evidence.quote: Must have either extensions or value[x], not both

examples.examplesMd: A useful negative test is an extension object that contains both nested `extension` and `valueString`. That fragment is not a valid R4 or R6 extension when the `Extension` StructureDefinition is applied; it is mentioned only to test whether an R6 validator incorrectly relies solely on Element.extension's inline constraints.

findings.narrativeMd: The local Element shape of `extension` did not change, but the R4 snapshot copied the `Extension` rule `ext-1` onto `Element.extension` while the R6 snapshot does not. Implementers who flatten a resource's snapshot and enforce only constraints physically present on each element could silently stop enforcing a core extension invariant. Implementers who validate each child according to its declared `Extension` type should see no instance-level semantic change.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not an old-valid/new-invalid break. If anything, a naive R6 snapshot-only validator could become too permissive and accept invalid extension content that R4 snapshot-only tooling rejected. Such falsely accepted R6 content would fail R4 validation and should fail R6 validation once `Extension.ext-1` is applied, so the main compatibility issue is validation completeness rather than representability of valid instances.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Validators and schema generators should not assume that all type-owned constraints are duplicated at every usage site. When processing `Element.extension`, dereference type `Extension` and apply the constraints on `Extension`, especially `ext-1`. Regression tests should include extensions with nested extensions only, value only, and both nested extension plus value to ensure invalid combinations are rejected.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping `ext-1` inline would have been a straightforward backward-compatible packaging choice for R4-style snapshot consumers. Removing the duplicate may be cleaner if R6 expects validators to compose constraints through type references, but that expectation needs to be explicit to avoid permissive validation behavior.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should confirm from official R6 narrative or tooling guidance whether this omission is intentional snapshot composition behavior. Do not interpret this finding as saying R6 permits extensions to contain both `extension` and `value[x]`; the R6 `Extension` artifact still forbids that.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Element.extension keeps the same cardinality, type, slicing, and modifier status, so there is no forward instance rejection for valid R4 data. The concern is that R4's Element snapshot carried the Extension-owned ext-1 invariant inline, while R6's Element snapshot does not. If R6 validators are expected to compose constraints through the declared Extension type, behavior is unchanged; if common tooling validates only the usage-site snapshot, malformed extensions could be accepted. Local package evidence shows the rule still exists on Extension, but not enough evidence was found here to decide whether the missing inline copy is intentional safe packaging or a compatibility-sensitive omission.
keyEvidence: R4 Element.extension constraint list includes ext-1 from http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Extension with expression extension.exists() != value.exists().
R6 Element.extension still has type Extension and open url slicing but its constraint list contains ele-1 only.
R6 StructureDefinition-Extension.json still defines ext-1 as an error invariant at Extension root.
No official Element/Extension snapshot-composition rationale or validator behavior evidence was available in the local inputs reviewed.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Element is normative and extensions are a universal mechanism, so a packaging change that could affect enforcement of ext-1 has a higher stability burden. That supports not dismissing the finding, but the remaining uncertainty is about intended validator composition rather than FMM.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: snapshot-only validators, schema generators, or flattened constraint indexes may stop enforcing ext-1 at Element.extension; type-aware validation through Extension should have no compatibility break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could keep ext-1 copied onto Element.extension, possibly marked as inherited or informational, while retaining Extension as the authoritative source. That would protect snapshot-only tools, but it duplicates a type-owned rule and can create stale-copy or precedence ambiguity. Whether that tradeoff is worthwhile depends on official R6 snapshot policy and validator expectations.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing medium runtime-impact and partial-alternative view, but the fresh review stops at Unclear because the decisive evidence is the intended R6 snapshot-composition contract, not just the local JSON delta.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, status, and abstract flag remain stable. The explicit R6 `Base` superclass is reported as a finding.
The snapshot element ids are unchanged: `Element`, `Element.id`, and `Element.extension`. No local add/remove/rename/move was found.
`Element.id` remains FHIRPath/System string and `Element.extension` remains type `Extension`. No local choice type change was found on Element.
Element has no Reference-typed local elements.
Element has no local terminology bindings in either StructureDefinition.
No validation expression strengthening was found for `ele-1`; the expression is unchanged. Constraint representation and usage-site packaging changes are reported separately.
No fixed, pattern, or default values were found on local Element elements.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraints were found.
`Element.id` and `Element.extension` remain `isSummary: false`; the root summary flag remains absent.
`Element.extension` remains open-sliced by `url` with discriminator type `value`.

Core definitions and comments are materially stable. R6 clarifies `ele-1` human text and changes the `Element.extension` definition spelling/spacing (`manageable` to `managable`), which was not treated as a breaking semantic change.
The XML attribute representation of `Element.id` is unchanged. Constraint serialization metadata changes, especially missing XPath, are reported separately.
No new local serialized Element child was added in R6, so ordinary valid R6 Element content maps to the same local R4 shape. Runtime metadata hierarchy differences still need tooling support.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: ele-1 human text now explicitly says value, children, or both
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The FHIRPath expression is unchanged, and logical `or` already allowed both value and children in R4. The R6 text is a clarification rather than a stricter rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation and test names that paraphrase `ele-1` should use the clearer R6 wording, especially for primitive values with extensions.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Administrative metadata updated without changing artifact identity
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds or updates metadata such as `experimental: false`, jurisdiction, publisher, contact, date, generated narrative, and the FHIR Infrastructure work-group extension. These do not change local instance validation for Element.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Package consumers that display maturity/work-group metadata may show different values in R6, but parsers and instance converters should not treat these as data-shape changes.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Element` now specializes `Base`. The Base report should own any findings about Base's own semantics and downstream hierarchy patterns beyond Element's local baseDefinition change.

`Element.extension` is typed as `Extension`, and the R6 Element snapshot no longer inlines `ext-1`. The Extension report should confirm all Extension-local constraint and choice-type changes, including any R6 value[x] additions.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 Element diff, migration note, or change rationale was available in the local inputs, so justification assessments are inferred from the computable StructureDefinitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official HL7 R6 ballot change notes, generated comparison pages, or Jira tickets for Element/Base/Extension infrastructure changes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 StructureDefinition contains generated narrative, but full specification prose for Element, Base, and extensibility rules was not separately reviewed. This most affects interpretation of whether the `Element.extension` ext-1 omission is intended snapshot composition behavior.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the published R6 Element and extensibility narrative pages and validator implementation guidance.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The new input is an R6 ballot build (`6.0.0-ballot4`) rather than a final published release, so details may change before final R6 publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the comparison against the final R6 core package when published.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No terminology expansion comparison was performed because `Element` has no local terminology bindings in the compared StructureDefinitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: No terminology follow-up is needed for Element unless profiles add bindings outside the base artifact.
